limitations: 30 synthetic clients publishing small text changes, not 30 LLM coding sessions or a 100-agent qualification.
Certificates and owners are distinct; profiles share the per-host OS account. Hostile processes sharing that account are not isolated.
The broker serializes publication and returns generic rejected_or_busy responses; this run does not classify every HTTP 409 cause.
Current publisher supports regular UTF-8 additions/updates only, bounded to 32 files and 64 KiB per request.
Single broker host and Mac login-session observer; no availability or renewal qualification.
Sandbox native Actions tested its existing Rust and workflow fixtures; new Python broker suites ran natively on four platforms, not on the recovery branch hosted CI.
Full Rust suite and binary smoke tests were not repeated because core Rust and binaries are unchanged.
No complete post-MIT feature parity or provenance-audit conclusion follows from this broker test.
